summary: Even on the way to the punishment, the court keeps trying to save the person. A man waits with a flag and another on a horse, ready to stop everything if anyone finds a new reason to say "not guilty."

chunks.en: When the case is finished,
chunks.st: When the trial has ended
chunks.stMore: in a guilty verdict and the condemned man has been sentenced to be stoned,

chunks.en: they take him out for his punishment of stoning.
chunks.st: he is taken out to be stoned.

chunks.he: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: The place of stoning was outside the court,
chunks.st: The place of stoning was outside the court and a little beyond it,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to a blasphemer:

chunks.en: "Take out the one who cursed."
chunks.st: “Take out him who has cursed
chunks.stMore: to outside the camp, and let all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let all the congregation stone him” (Leviticus 24:14).

chunks.he: אֶחָד עוֹמֵד עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית דִּין
chunks.en: One man stands at the door of the court
chunks.st: One man stands at the entrance to the court,

chunks.en: with flags in his hand,
chunks.st: with cloths [vehasudarin] in his hand,

chunks.en: and another man rides a horse
chunks.st: and another man sits on a horse

chunks.en: far away from him, but where he can still see him.
chunks.st: at a distance from him but where he can still see him.

chunks.en: If one of the judges says,
chunks.st: If one of the judges says:

chunks.en: "I have a reason to say he is not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to acquit him,

chunks.en: that man waves the flags,
chunks.st: the other, i.e., the man with the cloths, waves the cloths as a signal to the man on the horse,

chunks.en: and the horse runs and stops them.
chunks.st: and the horse races off after the court agents who are leading the condemned man to his execution, and he stops them,
chunks.stMore: and they wait until the court determines whether or not the argument has substance.

chunks.en: And even if he himself says,
chunks.st: And even if he, the condemned man himself, says:

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לִי לְלַמֵּד עַל עַצְמִי זְכוּת,
chunks.en: "I have a reason to say I am not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to acquit myself,

chunks.he: מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתוֹ אֲפִלּוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה פְעָמִים,
chunks.en: they bring him back, even four or five times,
chunks.st: he is returned to the courthouse, even four or five times,

chunks.en: as long as there is real sense in his words.
chunks.st: provided that there is substance to his words.
chunks.stMore: If, after the condemned man is returned to the courthouse, the judges

chunks.en: If they found a reason he is not guilty, they let him go.
chunks.st: find a reason to acquit him, they acquit him and release him immediately.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: But if they do not find a reason to acquit him,

chunks.en: he goes out for his punishment.
chunks.st: he goes out to be stoned.

chunks.en: And a man calls out in front of him:
chunks.st: And a crier goes out before him and publicly proclaims:

chunks.en: "So-and-so, the son of so-and-so,
chunks.st: So-and-so, son of so-and-so,

chunks.he: יוֹצֵא לִסָּקֵל עַל שֶׁעָבַר עֲבֵרָה פְלוֹנִית,
chunks.en: is going out to be punished for doing such-and-such a sin,
chunks.st: is going out to be stoned because he committed such and such a transgression.

chunks.en: and so-and-so and so-and-so are his witnesses.
chunks.st: And so-and-so and so-and-so are his witnesses.

chunks.en: Anyone who knows a reason to say he is not guilty
chunks.st: Anyone who knows of a reason to acquit him

chunks.en: should come and say it."
chunks.st: should come forward and teach it on his behalf.

summary: Before his punishment, the person is told to do teshuvah and confess his sins, so he will have a share in Olam Haba. We learn this from Achan in the days of Yehoshua.

chunks.he: הָיָה רָחוֹק מִבֵּית הַסְּקִילָה כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: When he was about ten amos from the place,
chunks.st: When the condemned man is at a distance of about ten cubits from the place of stoning,

chunks.en: they say to him, "Confess your sins,"
chunks.st: they say to him: Confess your transgressions,

chunks.en: because that is the way of those who are punished: they confess.
chunks.st: as the way of all who are being executed is to confess.

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּל הַמִּתְוַדֶּה יֶשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
chunks.en: Because anyone who confesses has a share in Olam Haba.
chunks.st: As whoever confesses and regrets his transgressions has a portion in the World-to-Come.

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְעָכָן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: That is what we find with Achan, when Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: For so we find with regard to Achan, that Joshua said to him:

words.note: He took things from Yericho that Hashem had forbidden.

chunks.he: בְּנִי שִׂים נָא כָבוֹד לַה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
chunks.en: "My son, please give honor to Hashem, the God of Yisrael,
chunks.st: “My son, please give glory to the Lord, God of Israel,

chunks.en: and confess to Him..."
chunks.st: and make confession to Him” (Joshua 7:19). And the next verse states:

chunks.en: And Achan answered Yehoshua and said,
chunks.st: “And Achan answered Joshua, and said:

chunks.he: אָמְנָה אָנֹכִי חָטָאתִי לַה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
chunks.en: "It is true, I sinned to Hashem, the God of Yisrael,
chunks.st: Indeed I have sinned against the Lord, God of Israel,

chunks.en: and this and that I did."
chunks.st: and like this and like that have I done.”

chunks.en: And how do we know his confession got him forgiveness?
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that Achan’s confession achieved atonement for him?

chunks.en: As it says,
chunks.st: It is derived from here, as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And Yehoshua said, Why did you bring trouble on us?
chunks.st: “And Joshua said: Why have you brought trouble on us?

chunks.en: Hashem will trouble you on this day."
chunks.st: The Lord shall trouble you this day” (Joshua 7:25).

chunks.en: This day you are troubled,
chunks.st: Joshua said to Achan as follows: On this day of your judgment you are troubled,

chunks.en: but you are not troubled in Olam Haba.
chunks.st: but you will not be troubled in the World-to-Come.

chunks.en: And if he does not know how to confess,
chunks.st: And if the condemned man does not know how to confess, either from ignorance or out of confusion,

chunks.en: they say to him,
chunks.st: they say to him:

chunks.he: אֱמֹר תְּהֵא מִיתָתִי כַפָּרָה עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָי.
chunks.en: "Say: May my death be a kaparah for all my sins."
chunks.st: Say simply: Let my death be an atonement for all my sins.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if he knew that the witnesses lied about him,
chunks.st: If the condemned man knows that he was convicted by the testimony of conspiring witnesses, but in fact he is innocent,

chunks.he: אוֹמֵר תְּהֵא מִיתָתִי כַּפָּרָה עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתַי
chunks.en: he says, "May my death be a kaparah for all my sins
chunks.st: he says: Let my death be an atonement for all my sins

chunks.en: except for this sin."
chunks.st: except for this sin.

chunks.en: They said to him, "If so,
chunks.st: The Sages who disagreed with Rabbi Yehuda said to him: If so,

chunks.en: everyone would say that
chunks.st: every person who is being executed will say that,

chunks.en: to make themselves look innocent."
chunks.st: to clear himself
chunks.stMore: in the eyes of the public. Therefore, if the condemned man does not make such a statement on his own, the court does not suggest it to him as an alternative.

summary: Close to the place of the punishment, his clothes were taken off. Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages argue about how a man and a woman are covered for modesty.

chunks.he: הָיָה רָחוֹק מִבֵּית הַסְּקִילָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: When he was four amos from the place,
chunks.st: When the condemned man is at a distance of four cubits from the place of stoning,

chunks.en: they take off his clothes.
chunks.st: they take off his clothes.

chunks.en: A man is covered in front,
chunks.st: They cover a man’s genitals in the front,

chunks.en: and a woman in front and in back.
chunks.st: and a woman is covered both in the front and in the back;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: But the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: a man is punished without his clothes,
chunks.st: A man is stoned naked, i.e., wearing only that cloth covering,

chunks.en: but a woman is not punished without her clothes.
chunks.st: but a woman is not stoned naked, but is stoned while clothed.

summary: This mishnah describes how the punishment of stoning was done, and which people were hung up afterward. The body must be taken down and buried the same day, so that Hashem's name is not shamed.

chunks.he: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה גָבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי קוֹמוֹת.
chunks.en: The place of stoning was twice as high as a person.
chunks.st: The place of stoning from which the condemned man is pushed to his death is a platform twice the height
chunks.stMore: of an ordinary person. He is made to stand at the edge of the platform, and then

chunks.he: אֶחָד מִן הָעֵדִים דּוֹחֲפוֹ עַל מָתְנָיו.
chunks.en: One of the witnesses pushes him down.
chunks.st: one of the witnesses who testified against him pushes him down by the hips, so that he falls face up onto the ground.

chunks.en: If he turned onto his front,
chunks.st: If he turned over onto his chest, with his face downward,

chunks.en: he turns him onto his back.
chunks.st: the witness turns him over onto his hips.

chunks.en: If he died from this, that is enough.
chunks.st: And if he dies through this fall to the ground, the obligation to stone the transgressor is fulfilled.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if the condemned man does not die from his fall,

chunks.en: the second witness takes the stone
chunks.st: the second witness takes the stone that has been prepared for this task

chunks.en: and drops it on him.
chunks.st: and places, i.e., casts, it on his chest.

chunks.en: If he died from this, that is enough.
chunks.st: And if he dies with the casting of this first stone, the obligation to stone the transgressor is fulfilled.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: And if he does not die with the casting of this stone,

chunks.en: it is finished by all Yisrael,
chunks.st: then his stoning is completed by all of the Jewish people,
chunks.stMore: i.e., by all the people who assembled for the execution,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: יַד הָעֵדִים תִּהְיֶה בּוֹ בָרִאשֹׁנָה לַהֲמִיתוֹ
chunks.en: "The hand of the witnesses shall be first against him,
chunks.st: “The hand of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death,

chunks.en: and the hand of all the people afterward."
chunks.st: and afterward the hand of all the people” (Deuteronomy 17:7).

chunks.en: Everyone who is stoned is hung up after he dies.
chunks.st: The corpses of all those who are stoned are hung after their death;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: only the one who cursed Hashem is hung,
chunks.st: Only the corpse of the blasphemer, who has cursed God,

chunks.en: and the one who served idols.
chunks.st: and the corpse of the idol worshipper are hung.

chunks.he: הָאִישׁ תּוֹלִין אוֹתוֹ פָּנָיו כְּלַפֵּי הָעָם,
chunks.en: A man is hung facing the people,
chunks.st: The corpse of a man is hung facing the people,

chunks.en: and a woman facing the wood,
chunks.st: but the corpse of a woman, out of modesty, is hung with facing the tree;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: a man is hung, but a woman is not hung.
chunks.st: the corpse of a man is hung, but the corpse of a woman is not hung.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Rabbis:

chunks.en: "But Shimon ben Shatach
chunks.st: Did Shimon ben Shataḥ not

words.note: A great leader in the time of the second Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: hang women in Ashkelon!"
chunks.st: hang in Ashkelon women
chunks.stMore: who were found guilty of witchcraft, proving that the corpse of a woman who is executed is also hung?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to him: No proof can be brought from here, as

chunks.en: "He hung eighty women,
chunks.st: he hanged eighty women on that day,

chunks.en: and a court may not judge two people on the same day."
chunks.explain: So that was a special punishment for a very hard time.
chunks.st: and the halakha is that the same court may not judge even two people charged with capital transgressions on the same day.
chunks.stMore: It is therefore clear that he was not acting in accordance with Torah law, but rather his execution of the eighty women was an extraordinary punishment necessitated by unusually pressing circumstances.

chunks.en: How do they hang him?
chunks.st: How do they hang
chunks.stMore: the corpse of one who was put to death by stoning?

chunks.en: They put a pole into the ground
chunks.st: They sink a post into the earth

chunks.en: with a piece of wood sticking out of it,
chunks.st: with a piece of wood jutting out, forming a T-shaped structure.

chunks.he: וּמַקִּיף שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו זוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי זוֹ
chunks.en: and he puts his two hands one on top of the other
chunks.st: And the court appointee then places the dead man’s two hands one upon the other, ties them,

chunks.en: and hangs him.
chunks.st: and hangs him by his hands.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: the pole leans on the wall,
chunks.st: The post is not sunk into the ground; rather, it leans against a wall,

chunks.en: and he hangs him the way butchers hang meat.
chunks.st: and he hangs the corpse on it the way that butchers do with meat.

chunks.en: And they untie him right away.
chunks.st: The dead man hangs there for only a very short time, and then they immediately untie him.

chunks.en: And if he stayed there overnight,
chunks.st: And if he was left hanging overnight,

chunks.en: they break a mitzvah of the Torah,
chunks.st: a prohibition is transgressed,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "His body shall not stay overnight on the wood,
chunks.st: “His body shall not remain all night upon the tree,

chunks.en: but you shall surely bury him,
chunks.st: but you shall bury him that day,

chunks.en: because one who is hung is a shame to Hashem."
chunks.st: for he that is hung is a curse of God” (Deuteronomy 21:23).

chunks.en: This means: Why is this one hung?
chunks.st: That is to say: Were the corpse left hanging on the tree overnight, people would ask: For what reason was this one hung
chunks.stMore: after he was put to death? They would be answered:

chunks.en: Because he cursed Hashem.
chunks.st: Because he blessed God, a euphemism for blasphemy.

words.note: This is a polite way to say "cursed."

chunks.en: And so Hashem's name would be shamed.
chunks.st: And therefore the name of Heaven would be desecrated
chunks.stMore: were the dead man’s corpse to remain hanging, reminding everybody of his transgression.

summary: Hashem feels pain even when a wicked person is punished, and even more for a tzaddik. So we must not leave anyone unburied overnight, except to honor him. Those punished by the court were buried in special places.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:
chunks.stMore: The phrase “for he that is hung is a curse [kilelat] of God” should be understood as follows:

chunks.en: when a person is in pain,
chunks.st: When a man suffers in the wake of his sin,

chunks.en: what does the Shechinah say, so to speak?
chunks.st: what expression does the Divine Presence use?

chunks.en: "My head is heavy,
chunks.st: I am distressed [kallani] about My head,

chunks.en: my arm is heavy."
chunks.explain: It means: I too am in pain.
chunks.st: I am distressed about My arm,
chunks.stMore: meaning, I, too, suffer when the wicked are punished.

chunks.en: If Hashem is in pain
chunks.st: From here it is derived: If God suffers such distress

chunks.en: about the blood of wicked people that was spilled,
chunks.st: over the blood of the wicked that is spilled,
chunks.stMore: even though they justly deserved their punishment, it can be inferred

chunks.he: קַל וָחֹמֶר עַל דָּמָם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים.
chunks.en: how much more so about the blood of tzaddikim!
chunks.st: a fortiori that He suffers distress over the blood of the righteous.

chunks.en: And not only this,
chunks.st: And the Sages said not only this,
chunks.stMore: that an executed transgressor must be buried on the same day that he is killed,

chunks.en: but anyone who leaves his relative who passed away unburied overnight
chunks.st: but they said that anyone who leaves his deceased relative overnight with-out burying him

chunks.en: breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
chunks.st: transgresses a prohibition.

chunks.he: הֱלִינוֹ לִכְבוֹדוֹ לְהָבִיא לוֹ אָרוֹן וְתַכְרִיכִים,
chunks.en: If he waited overnight for his honor, to bring him a coffin and shrouds,
chunks.st: But if he left the deceased overnight for the sake of the deceased’s honor, e.g., to bring a coffin or shrouds for his burial,

chunks.en: he does not break it.
chunks.st: he does not transgress
chunks.stMore: the prohibition against leaving him unburied overnight.

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּקִבְרוֹת אֲבוֹתָיו,
chunks.en: They would not bury him in the graves of his fathers,
chunks.st: After the executed transgressor is taken down he is buried, and they would not bury him in his ancestral burial plot.

chunks.en: but two graveyards
chunks.st: Rather, two graveyards

chunks.en: were set up for the court,
chunks.st: were established for the burial of those executed by the court:

chunks.en: one for those killed by the sword and by choking,
chunks.st: One for those who were killed by decapitation or strangled,

chunks.en: and one for those stoned and burned.
chunks.st: and one for those who were stoned or burned.

summary: Later the family gathered the bones and buried them in the family's place. The relatives would greet the judges and witnesses to show they were not angry, because the judgment was true.

chunks.en: After a long time, when only bones were left,
chunks.st: Once the flesh of the deceased had decomposed,

chunks.he: מְלַקְּטִין אֶת הָעֲצָמוֹת וְקוֹבְרִין אוֹתָן בִּמְקוֹמָן.
chunks.en: they gather the bones and bury them in their proper place.
chunks.st: they would gather his bones and bury them in their proper place in his ancestral burial plot.

chunks.en: And the relatives come and greet the judges
chunks.st: And soon after the execution, the relatives of the executed transgressor would come and inquire about the welfare of the judges

chunks.en: and greet the witnesses,
chunks.st: and about the welfare of the witnesses,

chunks.en: as if to say, "We have nothing in our hearts against you,
chunks.st: as if to say: We hold no grudges against you,

chunks.en: because you judged a true judgment."
chunks.st: as you judged a true judgment.

chunks.en: And they would not keep the halachos of mourning,
chunks.st: And the relatives of the executed man would not mourn
chunks.stMore: him with the observance of the usual mourning rites, so that his unmourned death would atone for his transgression;

chunks.en: but they would feel sad,
chunks.st: but they would grieve over his passing,

chunks.en: because sadness is only in the heart.
chunks.st: since grief is felt only in the heart.
